newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco panel backs stadium bond proposal.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco panel backs stadium bond proposal.

text.p: San Francisco's finance committee on Wednesday backed a resolution that would place a bond measure on the ballot to raise $100 million for a proposed football stadium and retail complex.
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors' finance committee recommended that the full board approve the proposal, which would place the lease-revenue bond measure on the June 3 special election ballot.
The full board will review the proposal next week.

If approved by San Francisco voters in June, the ballot proposition would authorize the city to issue the lease-revenue bonds in a principal amount not exceeding $100 million to finance a portion of the sports project.

The entire project is expected to cost $537 million, including $250 million for a proposed stadium for the National Football League 49ers, and $200 million for a proposed entertainment and shopping complex.
The resolution that advanced on Wednesday included several amendments. One would require certification that the total net proceeds of the bonds does not exceed $100 million.

Other amendments approved by the finance committee would require the 49ers to play all of their home games in the stadium until the retirements of the city's debt as well as a commitment that the city will be responsible for no more than 50 percent of the football-related operations and maintenance expenses of the stadium.
